title: Mugwort steam for period cramps
subtitle: An external steam preparation of Artemisia vulgaris for menstrual cramping
excerpt: Mugwort steam is a basin of just-boiled water with dried mugwort leaf, used as an external steam applied to the lower abdomen for menstrual cramps. A warming external preparation from traditional European and East Asian herbal practice. Mugwort is an emmenagogue and is strictly for use during a period already in progress, never in pregnancy. One session uses 2 to 3 tablespoons of dried leaf.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931), mugwort entry, Botanical.com. Nicholas Culpeper, Complete Herbal (1653), mugwort entry, public domain. Traditional East Asian moxa-warm application practices, documented in WHO monographs on selected medicinal plants vol. 1 (1999), Folium Artemisiae Argyi.

glossaryTerms.definition: A herb or preparation traditionally used to stimulate or encourage menstrual flow. Emmenagogues are contraindicated in pregnancy because the same stimulating action that brings on a period can affect a pregnancy.

content.text: Mugwort steam is a basin of just-boiled water with a generous handful of dried mugwort leaf, held close to the lower abdomen for 15 to 20 minutes. A warming preparation, not a vaginal steam, used in both European and East Asian herbal traditions for menstrual cramps during a period. attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor before use. Full precautions are in the 'When not to use' section.

content.text: Place 3 tablespoons of dried mugwort in a large heatproof bowl. Pour 500 ml of just-boiled water over the herb.

Sit in a position where you can hold the bowl close to your lower abdomen, with the steam rising towards the skin. Keep the bowl at a comfortable distance, do not allow the hot water or steam to contact skin directly.
Allow the steam to warm the lower abdomen for 15 to 20 minutes. Cover yourself with a blanket or towel around the bowl to keep the warmth directed at the target area.
Rest afterwards. A warm hot-water bottle to the lower abdomen follows on well from the steam.
Once or twice during the cramping phase of menstruation, as needed. This is an acute preparation, use when cramps are present, not as a daily routine.
Dried mugwort leaf stores 12 months in a sealed tin away from light and heat. Prepare each session fresh.
When not to use this remedy

Do not use in pregnancy. See a doctor for severe period pain that disrupts daily life or is getting worse. Also see a doctor if pain comes with heavy bleeding, pain during or after sex, or pain between periods. These may indicate endometriosis, fibroids, or pelvic infection.
